0.reason: the refusal wording for a missing absolute program is imprecise but harmless; it still names the missing path

findings.text: non-blocking: an absolute program that does not exist is refused with "names no executable under the run's checkout and repository (/opt/nope/python)", which states a resolution that never happened — an absolute path is candidates=(expanded,) and is never joined to a root — so the refusal misinforms the coordinator about where the program was looked for.

non-blocking: the "or failing that the repository" half of the deliverable has no test — all four cases record worktree == repo, so dropping the repo root from this tuple would leave every test green while a run whose worktree was released could no longer resolve its program.

justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:415-421 resolves a relative program against the run's recorded worktree and repo, and the probe against the landed tree shows the checkout case passing with the process cwd elsewhere and the repository fallback working.
